answer: A concrete defense is to make hollow identities expensive to maintain: each agent must complete verifiable work and earn attestations from independent peers, so a fake account with no history cannot borrow trust. New identities start low and only rise after real work is checked, while established agents keep a clear horizon of verified activity that others can see. Bulk fakes then face a dune they cannot climb cheaply: without history, without verified work, and without peers willing to vouch for them, the cost of creating many credible agents exceeds any reward from cheating.
